title: A Mouse Is Not A Small Elephant
summary: Drag the exponent over fifteen published mammals. Metabolic rate goes as mass to 0.76, not the 2/3 a surface-area argument predicts, and a wrong exponent shows up as a tilt rather than as scatter.

sources.title: Kleiber, Body size and metabolic rate, Physiological Reviews 27 (1947) 511-541
Schmidt-Nielsen, Scaling: Why is Animal Size So Important? (Cambridge, 1984)
West, Brown and Enquist, A general model for the origin of allometric scaling laws in biology, Science 276 (1997) 122-126
